summary: SSE midflight connection preemption splits sentence and strips final stop token on large responses
environment: client: NodeSDK v1.3.2 behind corp-proxy v2.7 (CorpEdge WAF)
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that long SSE responses produced by open-llm-13B-v2 are being delivered with the final sentence split across a connection preemption. The last character (final period/stop token) is missing after reconnect and finalization. Impact: User-visible truncated sentence in production chat UX; downstream parsers treat the reply as incomplete. Reported frequency: ~3-5% for responses > 1200 tokens; spike seen during edge-proxy rebalances.

Observed behavior: When an SSE connection is preempted by the corp edge (CorpEdge v2.7) during a heavy response, the client receives an early partial event with a newline-terminated fragment. After the client reconnects and requests session continuation, the server emits remaining tokens but the very last stop token (".") is not present and there is no explicit end marker. The client's parser treats the message as incomplete.

Expected behavior: Reconnected session should produce a seamless concatenation with the final punctuation preserved and/or an explicit end event indicating finalization.

Customer impact: LexiAssist chat sessions show truncated last sentences for several enterprise customers; affects compliance-sensitive transcripts.

Workaround attempted by customer: Client-side re-request of the last 256 tokens and stitch attempt; partial success but application-level deduplication produced duplication in ~10% of re-fetches.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use NodeSDK v1.3.2 and start SSE stream to text-generation endpoint using open-llm-13B-v2 with max_tokens=1600 and stream=true
2) From same client host, trigger a corp-proxy graceful connection migration (simulate CorpEdge rebind) during heavy streaming (approx 400-1200 tokens emitted)
3) Observe initial SSE fragments delivered; client reconnects and issues resume request with original session id
4) Inspect final tokens: last character or punctuation is missing and no explicit end event is emitted
logs: [serving-runtime] 2026-03-10T09:15:22.361Z streaming: emitted tokens=1198 last-flush=\"...policy for handling terminal punctuation pending\"
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Khan (Support): Opened after LexiAssist Sandbox report; attached client trace and transcript snippets. Noted correlation with corp-proxy rebinds.
2026-03-10 - LexiAssist (Customer): We see truncated sentences roughly 1 in 25 streams; it's breaking downstream NLP rules. Can you confirm this is not a client bug?

2026-03-11 - Marco Diaz (SRE): Reproduced locally with a proxy rebind script. Looks like a race when the preemption flush occurs during kernel selection in serving-runtime. Captured binary boundaries; forwarding to runtime team.

2026-03-11 - Runtime Eng (Eve Park): Hypothesis: final token flush occurs concurrently with session handoff and the end-marker generation path is skipped if flush completes in preempt window. Collecting more traces and adding assert to finalization path.

2026-03-12 - Marco Diaz (SRE): Temporary mitigation: advise customer to enable client heartbeat and prefer websocket fallback until patch. Documented workaround in comment and assigned ENG-STREAM-125 for fix.
investigation_notes: Initial reproduction using local proxy simulating CorpEdge rebind reproduced truncated final punctuation consistently when migration happens within a 150-350ms window during final KV cache flush.
Trace correlation shows api-gateway issues resume request with offset one token greater than server recorded last-emitted index (off-by-one on resume path).
Binary boundary shows final event written to ephemeral buffer but end-marker path (emit '\\n[END]') cleared by preemption handler before socket frame completion.
No evidence of client-side parser drop; NodeSDK v1.3.2 shows full receipt of frames as delivered by socket.
resolution: Mitigation (2026-03-12): Instructed LexiAssist to switch to websocket fallback and enabled client heartbeat; this eliminated occurrences in customer's canary region.

Planned fix (ENG-STREAM-125): Add ordered finalization barrier in serving-runtime so that preemption path waits for terminal marker write or queues explicit end-event across handoff. Target patch rollout to staging 2026-03-16.
Post-fix verification plan: create load test with induced preemption windows and assert final punctuation preserved in 1000-run job; add a regression test to streaming e2e harness.
next_steps: 1) ENG to implement finalization barrier (owner: Eve Park) - due 2026-03-15
